questions.locator: Section on the foundations of India's DPI ecosystem
questions.source_excerpt: This convergence took shape as the JAM trinity. Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar enrolment and widespread mobile phone penetration created the base layer for India's digital public infrastructure ecosystem.
questions.question: What is the 'JAM trinity' described as the foundational base layer of India's Digital Public Infrastructure?
options: Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar enrolment, and Mobile phone penetration
Judiciary, Administration, and Media reforms
Jobs, Agriculture, and Manufacturing policy
Justice, Accountability, and Monitoring frameworks
questions.explanation: The PIB backgrounder names the JAM trinity as Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar enrolment, and mobile phone penetration -- the convergence of these three formed DPI's base layer, not the unrelated institutional or sectoral groupings in the other options.

questions.source_excerpt: Aadhaar introduced a biometric based digital identity platform for residents... As of March 2026, more than 144 crore Aadhaar numbers had been generated.
questions.question: What kind of identity platform does Aadhaar provide, as described in PIB's 2026 backgrounder on India's DPI?
options: A biometric-based digital identity platform for residents, with over 144 crore numbers generated as of March 2026
A purely paper-based identity card system with no biometric component
An identity system available exclusively to government employees
A blockchain-based cryptocurrency wallet identity
questions.explanation: The backgrounder describes Aadhaar as a biometric-based digital identity platform for residents, citing over 144 crore numbers generated as of March 2026 -- not a paper-only system, an employees-only scheme, or a cryptocurrency wallet.

questions.source_excerpt: Unified Payments Interface (UPI): UPI has transformed retail payments into a seamless digital experience... A total of 691 banks are live on the UPI platform... the International Monetary Fund, in its June 2025 report on growing retail digital payments, recognised UPI as the world's largest retail fast payment system by transaction volume.
questions.question: How did the International Monetary Fund characterise UPI in its June 2025 report, per PIB's DPI backgrounder?
options: As a failed experiment that most Indian banks have since abandoned
As the world's largest retail fast payment system by transaction volume
As a system usable only by government employees for salary disbursal
As a payment system limited exclusively to cross-border remittances
questions.explanation: The IMF's June 2025 report recognised UPI as the world's largest retail fast payment system by transaction volume -- the backgrounder reports strong bank adoption (691 banks live), not abandonment, a government-employee-only scope, or a cross-border-remittance-only design.

questions.locator: Section on UPI, domestic adoption statistics
questions.source_excerpt: In India, 81 percent by volume of total retail payment transactions are processed on UPI rails, making it the preferred mode for person to person as well as person to merchant [payments].
questions.question: What share of India's total retail payment transactions (by volume) does the PIB backgrounder attribute to UPI?
options: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 81 percent
About 99 percent
questions.explanation: The backgrounder states that 81 percent of total retail payment transactions by volume in India are processed on UPI rails -- not 25, 50, or 99 percent as offered in the distractor options.

questions.source_excerpt: Cross Border Expansion of UPI: India's payment infrastructure has crossed national boundaries. UPI is now [live in several countries, including] Brazil, Lesotho, Maldives, Mongolia, Malaysia.
questions.question: According to the PIB backgrounder, what recent trend has UPI shown beyond its domestic success?
options: It has been withdrawn from operation entirely due to security concerns
It has expanded across national boundaries, going live in a growing list of countries
It has been merged into a single global cryptocurrency network
It has been restricted to use only within Indian embassies abroad
questions.explanation: The backgrounder describes UPI's cross-border expansion into multiple countries as a real trend -- there is no mention of withdrawal for security reasons, merger into a cryptocurrency network, or restriction to embassy-only use.

questions.source_excerpt: DigiLocker: Launched in 2015, DigiLocker introduced a secure digital document wallet for citizens to retrieve critical lifelong records anytime and from anywhere. As of 5 March 2026, DigiLocker had 67.63 crore users.
questions.question: What is DigiLocker, as described in PIB's 2026 backgrounder on India's DPI?
options: A secure digital document wallet, launched in 2015, letting citizens retrieve lifelong records anytime and from anywhere
A physical locker system installed only at post offices
A cryptocurrency exchange platform regulated by the RBI
A subscription-based cloud storage service run by a private foreign company
questions.explanation: DigiLocker is described as a secure digital document wallet launched in 2015, giving citizens access to lifelong records from anywhere -- not a physical post-office locker, a cryptocurrency exchange, or a foreign private subscription service.

questions.source_excerpt: By March 2026, over 950 crore documents had been issued [through DigiLocker].
questions.question: What scale of document issuance does the PIB backgrounder attribute to DigiLocker by March 2026?
options: Fewer than 1 lakh documents issued in total
Over 950 crore documents issued
Exactly 100 documents issued per registered user, with no more allowed
DigiLocker does not issue documents; it only stores documents users already have
questions.explanation: The backgrounder cites over 950 crore documents issued through DigiLocker by March 2026 -- not a negligible count, a fixed 100-per-user cap, or a claim that DigiLocker never issues documents (it explicitly does, alongside storage).

questions.source_excerpt: citizens can use UMANG to access services such as EPFO balance and claims, PAN and Aadhaar services, DigiLocker access, utility bill payments, pension services, scholarship applications...
questions.question: What role does the UMANG app play within India's Digital Public Infrastructure, per the PIB backgrounder?
options: It functions as a unified access point letting citizens reach services like EPFO, PAN/Aadhaar, DigiLocker, utility payments, pensions, and scholarships from one app
It is a standalone banking app with no connection to any other government service
It exists solely to renew passports and nothing else
It is restricted to use by government employees applying for internal transfers
questions.explanation: UMANG is described as a unified access point spanning EPFO, PAN/Aadhaar services, DigiLocker, utility bill payments, pension services, and scholarship applications -- not a single-purpose banking or passport app, nor an employees-only internal tool.

questions.source_excerpt: Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC): Launched in 2022, ONDC is an open network designed to democratise digital commerce... As of December 2025, there are a total of 1.16 lakh+ retail sellers live on ONDC from over 630+ cities and towns across India.
questions.question: What is the stated goal of the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), and what is its reported scale as of December 2025?
options: To democratise digital commerce, with over 1.16 lakh retail sellers live across 630+ cities and towns
To create a single monopoly e-commerce platform that eventually replaces all others
To restrict online commerce to only five major metropolitan cities
To operate exclusively as a business-to-government procurement channel with no retail sellers
questions.explanation: ONDC's stated goal is to democratise digital commerce via an open network, reporting 1.16 lakh+ retail sellers across 630+ cities and towns as of December 2025 -- it is an open network rather than a monopoly platform, is not restricted to five metros, and is a retail-facing initiative distinct from government procurement platforms.

questions.source_excerpt: Government eMarketplace: The Government eMarketplace has digitised public procurement and widened participation in government contracting. It provides an online platform for transparent and efficient procurement... [with] orders worth over Rs 7.35 lakh crore.
questions.question: What is the Government eMarketplace (GeM), according to the PIB backgrounder?
options: An online platform digitising public procurement, widening participation in government contracting, with orders worth over Rs 7.35 lakh crore
A private online retail store selling only to foreign buyers
A recruitment portal exclusively for hiring central government schoolteachers
A stock exchange for trading shares of public sector undertakings
questions.explanation: GeM is described as digitising public procurement and widening participation in government contracting transparently and efficiently, with cumulative orders worth over Rs 7.35 lakh crore -- not a foreign-only private retailer, a teacher recruitment portal, or a PSU stock exchange.

questions.locator: Section on the India Stack concept
questions.source_excerpt: open APIs (Application Programming Interface) and public digital goods. Known as India Stack, it unlocks the core building blocks of identity, data and payments at population scale.
questions.question: What does the term 'India Stack' refer to in the PIB backgrounder on Digital Public Infrastructure?
options: A stack of physical government office buildings constructed in New Delhi
A set of open APIs and public digital goods unlocking core building blocks of identity, data, and payments at population scale
A pile of paper files awaiting digitisation in government archives
A private cloud storage product sold exclusively to foreign governments
questions.explanation: India Stack is described as open APIs and public digital goods that unlock identity, data, and payments building blocks at population scale -- a conceptual/technical framework, not a literal building stack, a paper-archive backlog, or a product sold only to foreign governments.

questions.locator: Section on international cooperation on India Stack
questions.source_excerpt: India has signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoU) and agreements with 24 countries for cooperation on India Stack and Digital Public Infrastructure... To facilitate structured cooperation, India Stack Global was established.

options: By signing MoUs and agreements with 24 countries on India Stack/DPI cooperation, structured through the establishment of India Stack Global
By requiring every partner country to physically relocate its government servers to India
By selling exclusive licensing rights to a single foreign private company
India has made no international agreements regarding its DPI model
questions.explanation: The backgrounder describes MoUs/agreements with 24 countries and the creation of 'India Stack Global' to structure this cooperation -- not a server-relocation requirement, an exclusive private licensing deal, or an absence of international agreements.

questions.question: How does the linkage between Aadhaar and Digital Signature Certificates (as described in CCA's eSign integration guidelines) connect digital signatures to India's Digital Public Infrastructure identity layer?
options: It has no connection at all -- Digital Signature Certificates never reference Aadhaar in any way

questions.locator: Synthesis across JAM trinity, UPI, DigiLocker, and ONDC sections
questions.source_excerpt: Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar enrolment and widespread mobile phone penetration created the base layer... Known as India Stack, it unlocks the core building blocks of identity, data and payments at population scale.
questions.question: Drawing together the JAM trinity, UPI, DigiLocker, and ONDC as described in the PIB backgrounder, what common design pattern do India's DPI components share?
options: Each is a closed, proprietary system with no interoperability across the others
Each builds on a shared, population-scale foundation (identity via Aadhaar, payments via UPI rails, or open protocols) that other services and private players can build on top of
